h: Tips for a high-flying day out
p: The museum is spread across several big halls, so pace yourselves. It's easy to spend the first hour gawping at the first few aircraft and then have to rush the rest. A good plan is to do a quick lap first to spot the bits your group is most excited about, then go back and take your time. Most visitors find a good half day is the minimum, and plenty of aviation fans stay from opening until they're politely shooed out.

The Aircraft Carrier Experience is worth building your visit around. It recreates the feel of a carrier deck and the busy world beneath it, giving you a sense of how cramped, noisy and organised life at sea had to be to launch and recover aircraft. Kids who've only seen carriers on the news tend to come out wide-eyed.

Keep an eye on the sky while you're there. Because RNAS Yeovilton is a busy working air station, you can never be quite sure what will be flying on the day, and that unpredictability is half the fun. Bring the camera, and maybe a pair of binoculars for the plane spotters in the family.

Who will love it? Anyone who served, anyone whose relatives did, families with youngsters who love machines, and grown-ups who still remember Concorde's sonic boom era. It's also a thoughtful place for remembrance, with stories of the crews who didn't come home.
Nearby, the National Trust's Montacute House and the hilltop views at Ham Hill Country Park are within an easy drive, giving you a gentler second half to a Somerset day.
